info.title: HonestHook API
info.description: Profiles and posts from the major social networks, through one API. One key, one response shape; rate limits, retries and platform changes are on us. Clean JSON for your app or your AI agent. We read the exact field each platform publishes, and return null when none exists. Plus a historical trend archive that answers what was trending, which cannot be reconstructed after the fact.

get.summary: Public profile on mastodon, with the exact follower count.
get.description:
One public profile, normalised into the same envelope as every other platform. Source: the account's own instance (official API, no key). Costs 1 credit; the answer is cached for an hour and a cache hit costs nothing (`cached: true`, `credits_used: 0`).

**`user@instance`, and the instance is required.** Mastodon is federated: `Gargron` alone identifies nobody, because a different person can hold that name on every server. A handle without an instance is refused with 400 rather than completed with a default server — completing it would return somebody else's profile with `success: true`. The instance must be a public DNS name: IP literals, ports and paths are refused. The handle comes back fully qualified, so the response value is a valid next request.

get.summary: Recent posts on threads
get.description: Posts recentes do proprio perfil no Threads, lidos do mesmo tipo de documento que threads/profile le -- mas o documento e BAIXADO DE NOVO: o cache e por endpoint+params, entao chamar as duas rotas para o mesmo handle busca duas vezes (medido 15/09/2026: 1,55s depois do profile contra 1,60s sem ele, cached:false nos dois). Devolve os posts que vieram na pagina, sem paginacao -- medido em tres handles: 4, 5 e 10. Nao aceita ?limit=. Post de terceiro citado no feed e excluido por user.username. Devolve likes, replies e reposts; quotes e sempre null (a fonte nao publica contagem de citacao). Nao devolve reshare_count (presente em 8 de 13 posts medidos) nem media_type (e inteiro e ainda nao foi decodificado).

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: Threads username, same shape as Instagram: letters, digits, dot and underscore.

200.description: Posts found. `has_more` differs by platform: on Bluesky it is computed from the cursor the source returns, so it can be true. On Mastodon it is false today because we do not yet read the `Link` header. On Threads it is null — the posts arrive inside the profile document and there is nothing to page, so we cannot know. `null` means unknown, never `no more`.

400.description: `parametro_invalido` — the handle is missing, does not match this platform's format, or `limit` is outside the range. Nothing is charged.

404.description: `nao_encontrado` — no such account. Nothing is charged.

get.summary: Recent posts on bluesky
get.description: Posts recentes do proprio perfil no Bluesky, via app.bsky.feed.getAuthorFeed -- API publica oficial do AT Protocol, sem chave e sem conta. Sai pelo servico de fetch como as demais rotas, entao consome banda de proxy: ~93 KB com limit=25. Aceita ?limit= de 1 a 100, padrao 25; valor fora da faixa e recusado com 400 em vez de aparado, e cada limite tem a sua propria linha de cache. Repost de terceiro e excluido por autoria (o feed do bsky.app traz 1 em 20). Devolve likes, replies, reposts e quotes; nao devolve bookmarkCount (so o Bluesky tem) nem thumbnail (o embed de imagem ainda nao foi medido em amostra suficiente).

parameters.name: handle
parameters.description: AT Protocol handle, which is a domain name: `bsky.app`, `alguem.bsky.social`. Dots are part of it; slashes are refused.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many posts to return, 1 to 100. A value outside the range is refused with 400, not clamped: the source clamps in silence, and a caller asking for more than the maximum would conclude the account has fewer posts than it does.

On Mastodon it is false today because we do not yet read the `Link` header. On Threads it is null — the posts arrive inside the profile document and there is nothing to page, so we cannot know. `null` means unknown, never `no more`.

get.summary: Recent posts on mastodon
get.description: Posts recentes do proprio perfil no Mastodon, via API oficial da instancia da conta (sem chave). O handle e SEMPRE usuario@instancia: o Mastodon e federado, e o nome sozinho nao identifica ninguem. Aceita ?limit= de 1 a 40, padrao 20; valor fora da faixa e recusado com 400 em vez de aparado -- a fonte apara em silencio, e quem pedisse 100 receberia 40 achando que a conta tem 40 posts. Boost (repasse de terceiro) NAO entra: sao 15 em cada 20 no feed cru, e o objeto de cima de um boost vem com texto vazio e metricas zeradas. Resposta a outra pessoa entra, porque foi a conta que escreveu. Devolve likes, replies, reposts e quotes. O corpo vem em DOIS campos: `text` ja limpo de HTML, e `text_html` com o original -- este ultimo e HTML de terceiro e precisa ser sanitizado antes de ir para uma pagina, sob risco de XSS. `title` e sempre null (status nao tem titulo) e `position` e sempre null (ordem cronologica nao e ranking).

get.summary: Story highlight covers of a public Instagram profile — id, title and cover.
get.description: The story highlight tray of a public Instagram profile: id, title and cover image for each highlight, read from the SAME logged-out profile page as instagram/profile. Measured on 2026-10-01 against the committed 829 KB page for nasa: 5 highlights, and has_next_page false -- so that is the whole tray, and has_more says so. Does NOT return the media inside a highlight: opening one needs a logged-in session, so no logged-out surface carries it. No date and no counter per highlight -- the tray has neither, so both are null. next_cursor is null even though the page carries an end_cursor: no parameter here accepts one, and paging the tray would mean calling Instagram GraphQL, another surface. position is null on purpose -- Instagram orders the tray by recent update, not the owner. Costs 1 credit and caches for an hour; the cache is per endpoint and params, so asking for profile and highlights on the same handle downloads the page twice.

get.summary: What an Instagram embed shows: the profile plus the thumbnails on its grid.
get.description: What an Instagram embed shows: the profile plus the posts that come on the public page itself -- caption, thumbnail, media type (image, video, carousel) and the post URL. NOT an alias of instagram/profile: it returns the list that route returns empty. NOT named posts either, because the */posts family here returns per-post counters and this page has none -- like_count, comment_count and play_count appear ZERO times in the 829 KB page, so metrics is null and never an empty object. published_at is null: the only date in the document is day-precision text inside localized alt text, sitting next to a third party name, and a guessed hour would be worse than nothing. Measured on 2026-10-01 for nasa: the grid carries 12 nodes and 7 belong to nasa -- the other 5 are collaborators (nasajohnson, astro_anil, jeopardy) and are dropped by user.username, the same filter threads/posts uses. has_more comes from the page own has_next_page and is true; there is no cursor to hand out. Costs 1 credit and caches for an hour; the cache is per endpoint and params, so the three Instagram routes on the same handle download the page three times.

get.summary: Recent posts tagged at a public Instagram location, plus the location itself.
get.description: Recent posts tagged at a public Instagram location, plus the location itself (name, slug, category and how many posts are tagged there). Order is what the platform served, NOT chronological. Views, reposts and quotes do not exist here. Anchored on the location id: a location that does not exist answers 404, never an empty list.

get.summary: The stories inside one public Instagram highlight, plus the highlight and its owner.
get.description: The stories inside one public Instagram highlight, oldest first (measured: chronological, unlike the location tab). Returns the highlight itself -- id, title, cover, how many stories -- plus the owner handle and whether that account is verified or private. Story view counts do not exist here: they are owner metrics and need a logged-in session. Anchored on the highlight id echoed back by the page, so a highlight that does not exist answers 404, never an empty list.

get.summary: A single public Instagram post, by its shortcode.
get.description: One public Instagram post by SHORTCODE, from instagram.com/p/{code}/ -- the logged-out page, no account of ours and none of a third party. THE PARSER ALREADY EXISTED WITH NO DOOR: normalizarPost has been in lib/normalize/instagram.js with a committed 934 KB fixture, and no route used it; this is the door, same as bluesky/post. Returns id, url, caption text, thumbnail_url, published_at and metrics with likes and comments -- measured on shortcode Db9IVmrDvQ4: 2445668 likes, 4703 comments. THE AUTHOR COMES BACK ALL NULL, and that is us not filling it in, NOT the platform lacking it: the document carries the owner (user appears 30 times), and normalizarPost does not extract it today -- saying the author is unknown would be a plausible value in the wrong place. title is null because an Instagram post has a caption, not a title, and inventing one from the first line of the caption would serve a guess as a field. A shortcode that does not exist is not reliably distinguishable from our own transport failing, which is why no result is never charged here.

get.summary: Public boards of a Pinterest account — name, description, pin count and followers.
get.description: The public boards of a Pinterest account: id, name, description, board URL, cover image, creation date, pin count and follower count for each one -- read from the SAME logged-out profile page as pinterest/profile. Measured on 2026-10-01 against the committed 1.3 MB page for nasa: 10 distinct boards, every one carrying all of those fields. Returns the SHELF, not the pins: the pins inside a board are not on this page, so listing them would be a different call. metrics carries pins and followers, never likes -- a board has no likes, and reusing the post field names would invite summing things that are not the same. published_at is the board creation date, parsed from an RFC 1123 string, not an epoch. Boards owned by someone else are dropped by owner.username, the same filter threads/posts uses. has_more and next_cursor are null: what the page carried is what exists, and paging would mean another surface. Costs 1 credit and caches for an hour; the cache is per endpoint and params, so asking for profile and boards on the same handle downloads the page twice.

get.summary: A single Bluesky post by its AT Protocol URI, with likes, reposts, replies and quotes.
get.description: A single Bluesky post, addressed by its AT Protocol URI (at://did:plc:.../app.bsky.feed.post/...). Returns the post as a one-item list, with likes, replies, reposts and quotes, plus the post author in the author envelope. Read from app.bsky.feed.getPostThread, the same public surface bluesky/profile uses -- no login, no third party. Measured on 2026-10-01 against the committed 289 KB thread fixture. Does NOT return the replies: the document carries 193 of them and we deliberately leave them out, because mixing a post with its replies in one list would make both unreadable; a replies endpoint would be its own call. There is no legitimate empty result here -- either the post was read or it was not, so a failure is an error and never an empty list, and a failed read is not charged. Followers and bio are null: this call does not carry them, which is different from the account not having them. title is null because a Bluesky post has none. Costs 1 credit and caches for an hour.

get.summary: Public Bluesky posts matching a term, ranked by top, with likes, reposts, replies and quotes.
get.description: Public Bluesky posts matching a TERM, via app.bsky.feed.searchPosts -- the official AT Protocol API, no key and no account. FOURTH and last Bluesky path of the parity grid. THE HOST IS api.bsky.app, NOT public.api.bsky.app, and that difference is the whole endpoint: public.api.bsky.app answers 403 with an HTML block page on this route while answering 200 on getAuthorFeed, so the block is per-host, not the endpoint asking for an account -- our own archiver has searched through api.bsky.app since 06/09/2026. Results come from MANY authors, so unlike bluesky/posts there is no authorship filter; filtering by author here would always return empty. sort=top, not latest: on a popular term latest is almost all noise. hitsTotal IS NOT RETURNED -- measured, it reads 10000 for a common term and 0 for a nonexistent one, so it is a search cap dressed as a total, and serving it would promise a count nobody measured; sample_size says how many THIS call brought. Accepts ?limit= from 1 to 100, default 25; out of range is 400, never silently clamped -- measured, the source REFUSES limit=101 with 400 instead of trimming. has_more is Boolean(cursor) and nothing else. A term with no result is 200 with an empty items list -- that is an answer, and it is charged.

get.summary: Public repositories of a GitHub account, with stars and forks.
get.description: Repositorios publicos de um usuario do GitHub, via API oficial. Campos com o NOME DA FONTE: stargazers_count, forks_count, open_issues_count, watchers_count, language, topics, license (SPDX), archived, fork, created_at, updated_at, pushed_at. Repositorio NAO e post: nada aqui vira metrics, e estrela nao e like. Conta sem repositorio responde items vazio e e cobrada; conta inexistente nao.

get.description: Serie historica de um perfil: uma linha por janela horaria em que o perfil foi consultado por alguem. Cobra 1 credito apenas quando ha pelo menos uma captura no intervalo.

get.summary: Hacker News stories matching a term, with points and comments.
get.description: Busca de historias no Hacker News por TERMO, via hn.algolia.com -- API publica, documentada, sem chave e sem conta. PRIMEIRA rota da casa que nao pergunta por uma pessoa: o parametro e ?q=, nao ?handle=. Usa o MESMO cliente HTTP do arquivador (lib/fontes/hackernews.js), que desde 05/09/2026 carrega o que custou caro descobrir: o Algolia nao interpreta OR, e com typoTolerance ligada o termo mrr devolvia 81 resultados e nenhum sobre MRR. Um segundo cliente devolveria ao cliente pagante o lixo que o arquivador aprendeu a recusar. Sem a janela de 48h do arquivador: quem busca quer o que existe, nao o que subiu anteontem. Aceita ?limit= de 1 a 100, padrao 25; fora da faixa e 400, nao aparado. Termo sem resultado e 200 com items vazio -- e uma resposta, e e cobrada. author NAO sai: existe na resposta do Algolia, esta na fixture de proposito, e o teste reprova se vazar.

get.summary: One Hacker News story by id — the story, not the comments.
get.description: UMA historia do Hacker News pelo id, via hn.algolia.com/api/v1/items/{id}. DESCARTA OS COMENTARIOS por decisao: medido em 30/09/2026 no item 46990729, a resposta tem 489.835 bytes e 176 comentarios, cada um com author e text de uma pessoa que nao e o cliente e nao pediu nada. Sobrevive metrics.comments, que e a CONTAGEM -- mede sem identificar; quando children nao vem e null, nunca 0. num_comments NAO existe neste endpoint (a busca tem o contador, o item nao), por isso a contagem sai de children.length. Comentario nao e historia: /items/{id} responde 200 para os dois, e o comentario vem com title null -- sem a ancora do normalizador o cliente receberia texto de terceiro com success true. Com ela, 404. id aceita ate 12 digitos e nada mais.

get.summary: Public Hacker News user: karma, the about text, and nothing invented.
get.description: A public Hacker News user via hn.algolia.com/api/v1/users/{handle}: karma and the about text, and nothing invented. KARMA IS ITS OWN FIELD, not followers. Hacker News has no follower graph -- followers, following and posts_count are all null here -- and mapping karma onto followers would put a plausible value in the wrong field, stable enough that a client comparing audience across platforms would read karma as reach. The anchor is handle, NEVER karma: a new account legitimately has karma 0, and treating 0 as absent would report a real user as missing. A user that does not exist is a real 404 and costs no credit.

get.summary: Comments on a Hacker News story, flattened, with depth and parent id.
get.description: The comments on a Hacker News story, flattened, each with depth and parent id. SAME UPSTREAM DOCUMENT as hackernews/story -- hn.algolia.com/api/v1/items/{id} already carries the comment tree in children, and the story route discards it on purpose. There is no new upstream call here; there is exposure of what already arrived. Measured on item 8863: 32 children, 104 points. An empty list is an answer (a story with no comments is charged, the question was answered); an id that does not exist is a real 404 and costs no credit. THE ANCHOR HERE IS id, NOT title: /items/{id} answers 200 for a story and for a comment alike, and this route requires only id -- measured, a comment id is accepted with 200 and comes back with the replies to THAT comment and title null. Whoever needs to tell a story from a comment has to read title in the response, because this route does not do it for them. The sibling route hackernews/story DOES refuse a comment, because it requires title.

get.summary: Search terms TikTok suggests for a keyword — the autocomplete list, ranked.
get.description: The search terms TikTok suggests for a keyword: the autocomplete list behind the search box, read logged-out from the site own preview endpoint. Takes keyword, not handle -- this endpoint answers about a TERM, not about a person, and author comes back with every field null on purpose. Each item carries the suggested term in title, a TikTok search URL built from that term, and the id of the term group; position is the rank TikTok gave it, counted from 1. metrics is always null: a suggestion has no counters, and zeros would claim it has counters that read zero. published_at is null for the same reason -- the endpoint sends no date, and stamping the request time would invent freshness. An empty list is an ANSWER: a keyword with no suggestion returns 200 with items: [] and is charged, because the question was answered. A body we could not read, a missing list, or an error status inside the body is a FAILURE and returns 404 without charging. has_more and next_cursor are null: this endpoint does not page, it sends no cursor and no total, and saying false would promise the list ended. Costs 1 credit and caches for 60 seconds only -- measured on 2026-10-01, 6 of 8 suggested terms for the same keyword changed within the hour, so an hour-long cache would serve a list the platform had already replaced.

get.summary: A single TikTok video by its URL, with caption, cover, date and counters.
get.description: One public TikTok video by its URL, read logged-out from the video page itself. Takes the FULL video address -- https://www.tiktok.com/@handle/video/1234567890123456789 -- and not an id on its own: the document lives under the handle, so an id without it cannot be addressed. items carries exactly one entry: the video id, its page URL, the caption in text, the cover image in thumbnail_url, the publication date parsed from an epoch in seconds, and metrics with likes, comments, shares, views and saves. title is null -- a video has no title, its caption is a body -- and position is null too, because a list of one has no meaningful order. author carries the id, handle, name, bio, avatar and verified flag the video page publishes, and followers, following and posts_count come back null ON PURPOSE: this page gives a follower count with no exact counterpart to check it against, while tiktok/profile reads the exact one; filling both from different sources would make two of our endpoints disagree about the same account. WARNING: THE LARGE COUNTERS ARE ROUNDED BY TIKTOK on this surface -- measured on 2026-10-02 against the committed capture, both of the page stat blocks agree on 2,000,000 likes and 5,500,000 views, so treat them as rounded to three significant figures and not as exact. A video that is restricted by its owner and an id that does not exist both answer 404 and are NOT charged: the page returns the same status code for the two, and only the status message tells them apart. has_more and next_cursor are null: the document is one video, there is no list to page. Costs 1 credit and caches for an hour -- the video itself does not change, and the counters that do are already rounded.

get.summary: The on-screen text of one TikTok video, one item per line, in reading order.
get.description: The on-screen text of one public TikTok video: the words burned on top of the frames, read logged-out from the video page itself. Takes the FULL video address -- https://www.tiktok.com/@handle/video/1234567890123456789 -- and not a bare id, because the page needs the handle in the path. Returns one item per line, in the order the document declares them, which is reading order on screen. This is NOT the caption and NOT the spoken audio: the caption is the text field of tiktok/post, and the spoken audio is a separate WEBVTT asset served by tiktok/post_transcript. Three different texts live in the same document and mixing them up would return plausible wrong data. Measured on 2026-10-01 across 10 reachable videos: 7 carry at least one line of on-screen text and 3 carry none. A video that exists and has no on-screen text answers with items: [] and IS charged -- the question was answered and the page was downloaded. A restricted, missing or unclassifiable video answers 404 and costs nothing. metrics, published_at and thumbnail_url are null on every item: a line of text has no date, no picture and no counter, and returning zeros would claim it has them. Costs 1 credit and caches for an hour. The cache is per endpoint and params, so asking for post and screen-text on the same video downloads the page twice.

get.summary: The spoken transcript of one TikTok video, as one item, without cue timings.
get.description: The spoken transcript of one public TikTok video, read logged-out. Takes the FULL video address -- https://www.tiktok.com/@handle/video/1234567890123456789 -- and not a bare id, because the page needs the handle in the path. This is the AUDIO, not the caption and not the words burned on the frames: the caption is the text field of tiktok/post and the on-screen words are tiktok/video_screen_text. Three different texts live in the same video and mixing them up would return plausible wrong data. HOW OFTEN IT EXISTS: measured on 2026-10-01 across 10 reachable videos, only 1 carried a subtitle track. A video with no track answers items: [] and IS charged -- the question was answered and the page was downloaded. Expect the empty answer to be the common one. The transcript comes back as ONE item whose text is the whole speech, because the source is a WEBVTT of automatic speech recognition and its cues are arbitrary time slices, not sentences -- one cue in the measured file is "and you need to stop being immature", mid-sentence. The cue TIMINGS are not published: this schema has no offset field, and inventing one per route is how an API starts speaking two languages. title carries the language the source declares (eng-US in the measurement) or null. id, published_at, thumbnail_url and metrics are null: speech has no identifier, no date, no picture and no counter. Reading it costs TWO network calls on our side -- the video page points at a file on another host -- and still 1 credit, because you asked for one thing. Caches for an hour, the same as tiktok/post and tiktok/video_screen_text, so asking for more than one of them on the same video downloads the page once per endpoint.

get.summary: One public YouTube video by id, with the exact view and like counts in metrics.views and metrics.likes.
get.description: One public YouTube video by id, read from the logged-out watch page. Returns the EXACT like count -- not the abbreviated one the interface shows next to it. The exact view count is read and NOT returned: the published metrics contract has four keys (likes, replies, reposts, quotes) and no views. replies is null because the page carries no comment count. The 20 recommended videos the page cites are discarded.

get.summary: The 50 most recent videos of a YouTube channel, with exact view, like and comment counts per video, from the official Data API. The RSS feed is the declared reserve for when the daily quota runs out, and it is not wired yet — see the route header.
get.description: The 50 most recent videos of a YouTube channel, from the official Data API v3 (channels.list + playlistItems.list + videos.list, 3 quota units). EXACT viewCount, likeCount and commentCount per video, plus duration and whether it is a live broadcast. The view count is read and NOT returned: the published metrics contract has four keys and views is not one of them. has_more is null, never false.

get.summary: The videos a public YouTube playlist feed carries, with exact views and likes per video — 15 at most, which is the feed's ceiling and not the playlist's size.
get.description: The videos a public YouTube playlist feed carries, with the exact like count per video. CEILING OF 15, and it is the feed's ceiling, not the playlist's size -- has_more is null because the feed does not say how long the playlist is. The playlist TITLE is not returned: the envelope has no field for a collection name, and author is the owning channel.

get.summary: The Shorts on a YouTube channel's Shorts tab, with titles and thumbnails.
get.description: The Shorts on a YouTube channel's Shorts tab, read from the logged-out page. Title, id and thumbnail per Short. The view count is NOT returned: the tab publishes it abbreviated and localised ("256K views"), and an abbreviated value becomes null here, never a reconstructed number -- call youtube/video by the id for the exact count. published_at is null too: the tab shows a relative date ("3 days ago").

get.summary: The streams on a YouTube channel's Live tab — past, in progress and scheduled in one list, and the state of each is not returned. A stream that is live right now carries metrics.watching, the exact number of people watching.
get.description: The streams on a YouTube channel's Live tab (served by YouTube at /streams). WARNING: past, in-progress and SCHEDULED streams come in one list and the state of each is NOT returned -- measured badges include LIVE and Upcoming. Call youtube/video by the id and read isLiveContent. No metric is returned: a scheduled stream has no views, and the tab metadata reads "N waiting" or "N watching" -- the second is an exact count of people watching right now, and it still does not fit: metrics has four keys and a concurrent viewer is none of them.

get.summary: The public playlists of a YouTube channel, with the exact video count of each, from the official Data API. A podcast may come through as a playlist.
get.description: The public playlists of a YouTube channel, from the official Data API v3 (channels.list + playlists.list, 2 quota units). metrics.videos is contentDetails.itemCount, an exact integer. WARNING: a podcast may come through as a playlist -- the resource has status.podcastStatus but its values were not read against a real response, and guessing the value of a field to decide what the client receives is not something we do.

get.summary: Top-level comments on a public YouTube video — text, date and like count. Who wrote each one is not returned.
get.description: Top-level comments on a public YouTube video, from the official Data API v3 (videos.list + commentThreads.list, 2 quota units). Returns the comment TEXT (textOriginal, not the HTML of textDisplay), the date and the like count -- and metrics.replies is totalReplyCount, which measures without identifying. WHO WROTE EACH COMMENT IS NOT RETURNED: the four author fields the API sends are read and discarded, because an item has no author field in this contract. The embedded replies.comments are not flattened into the list; call youtube/video/comment/replies with the comment id.

get.summary: Replies to one YouTube comment — text, date and like count. Who wrote each one is not returned.
get.description: Replies to one YouTube comment, from the official Data API v3 (comments.list?id= as the anchor + comments.list?parentId=, 2 quota units). Same contract as youtube/video/comments: text, date and like count, and who wrote each reply is not returned. The anchor is not optional -- parentId returns an empty list both for a parent with no replies and for an id that does not exist. The author of the envelope carries only the channel id: the comment resource has no channelTitle, and a name nobody asked for is not worth another quota unit.

get.summary: The videos in a YouTube playlist, from the official Data API v3 (playlists.list + playlistItems.list + videos.list, 3 quota units, 1 credit). EXACT viewCount, likeCount and commentCount per video. One page of up to 50 — the playlist's own size and `contentDetails.itemCount` are NOT returned, and has_more is null, never false. The playlist title is not returned either: the envelope's author is the owning channel.
get.description: The videos in a YouTube playlist, from the official Data API v3 (playlists.list + playlistItems.list + videos.list, 3 quota units). EXACT viewCount, likeCount and commentCount per video, in the order the playlist declares. The first call is the ANCHOR and it is not ceremony: the API answers 200 with items: [] for a playlist that does not exist, and playlistItems.list on a missing playlist returns the same empty list an empty playlist returns -- without it, 404 and "empty playlist" would be the same answer. One page of up to 50: the playlist size and contentDetails.itemCount are NOT returned, and has_more is null, never false. The playlist title is not returned either -- the envelope has no field for a collection name, so author is the owning channel.

get.summary: Every thumbnail the official Data API v3 declares for one YouTube video (videos.list, 1 quota unit, 1 credit), one item per size: id is the size name, metrics carries width and height. Only the sizes that video actually has are returned — no URL is ever built from a filename convention, so a size that is missing is absent rather than a guessed link. Nothing else about the video comes back.
get.description: Every thumbnail the official Data API v3 declares for one YouTube video (videos.list, 1 quota unit), one item per size: id is the size name (default, medium, high, standard, maxres) and metrics carries width and height. Only the sizes that video actually has come back -- NO url is ever built from a filename convention, so a size the response did not declare is absent rather than a guessed link that may 404. Nothing else about the video is returned: title, duration, views and likes are youtube/video.

get.summary: The videos trending in one region, from the official Data API v3 (videos.list with chart=mostPopular, 1 quota unit, 1 credit) — up to 50, in chart order, with exact view, like and comment counts. `region` is REQUIRED on purpose: trending does not exist without a region, and a silent default would publish one country's chart as if it were the world's. There is no author: the list belongs to a region, not to an account. has_more is null, never false, and no category name is returned.
get.description: The videos trending in one region, from the official Data API v3 (videos.list with chart=mostPopular, 1 quota unit) -- up to 50, in chart order, with exact view, like and comment counts. The region parameter is REQUIRED on purpose: trending does not exist without a region, and a silent default would publish one country's chart as if it were the world's. There is no author -- the list belongs to a region, not to an account, so the twelve author fields are null by decision. has_more is null, never false. The category is not returned: snippet carries a numeric categoryId whose meaning needs another call we do not make, and serving the raw number would serve a code the client cannot resolve.

get.summary: One YouTube channel plus its recent videos in a single answer, from the official Data API v3 (channels.list + playlistItems.list + videos.list, 3 quota units, 1 credit) — the channel in `author` with exact subscriber, video and view counts, and the recent uploads as items with exact view, like and comment counts. NO COMPUTED ANALYTICS ARE RETURNED: no average views per video, no engagement rate, no upload cadence, no growth. This is a COMPOSITION of two calls the client could make separately, saved as one request; every number in it is a number the source states. It does NOT use search.list. One page of recent uploads: `limit` is NOT accepted and has_more is null, never false.
get.description: One YouTube channel plus its recent videos in a single answer, from the official Data API v3 (channels.list + playlistItems.list + videos.list, 3 quota units) -- the channel in author with exact subscriber, video and view counts, and the recent uploads as items with exact view, like and comment counts. NO COMPUTED ANALYTICS ARE RETURNED: no average views per video, no engagement rate, no upload cadence, no growth. It is a COMPOSITION of calls the client could make separately, saved as one request; every number in it is a number the source states. It does NOT use search.list. One page of recent uploads -- limit is NOT accepted and has_more is null, never false.

get.summary: One public GitHub repository, with the source's own field names — stars, forks and open issues are not likes.
get.description: One public GitHub repository. Fields keep the SOURCE names -- stargazers_count, forks_count, open_issues_count, watchers_count, language, topics, archived, fork -- because a repository is not a post and a star is not a like. WARNING: watchers_count equals stargazers_count in the API; real watchers are in subscribers_count, which this endpoint does not return. A renamed repository answers 200 under its NEW name: we compare full_name with what you asked and give 404 if they differ, instead of serving the redirect silently.

get.summary: The issues of a GitHub repository AND its pull requests, which the API counts as issues — each item says which it is.
get.description: The issues of a GitHub repository AND its pull requests. The GitHub API counts every PR as an issue: MEASURED, 8 of the 10 items it returned were PRs. Each item carries is_pull_request (from the presence of the pull_request key) and a url that reads /pull/N or /issues/N. We do NOT filter the PRs out -- hiding 8 of 10 items would surprise more than labelling them. state=all, so closed issues come too.

get.summary: The README of a GitHub repository, decoded from the base64 the API returns.
get.description: The README of a GitHub repository, DECODED from the base64 the API returns. The endpoint resolves which file is the README (readme.md, README, .github/README.md) and the answer says which one it was, in name and path. If the API declares an encoding other than base64 -- which it does for large files -- content is null and encoding comes through as it arrived, instead of an empty string served as a README.

get.summary: The releases of a GitHub repository, each saying whether it is a prerelease — seven of ten measured were.
get.description: The releases of a GitHub repository. Every item says prerelease and draft, and that is not decoration: MEASURED, seven of ten were prereleases and the most recent one was a canary. assets is the COUNT of attached files, not the files. reactions keeps the GitHub names, and total_count is NOT likes -- measured, a release with total_count 3 had one +1 and two hooray.

get.summary: One GitHub issue or pull request by number — the same path serves both, and the item says which.
get.description: One GitHub issue OR pull request by number -- the same API path serves both and there is no issue-only endpoint. The item says which, through is_pull_request and through the url. number is REQUIRED and has no default: there is no such thing as a default issue, and guessing 1 would serve the wrong one with a 200.

get.summary: The conversation comments on a GitHub issue or pull request — text, date and reactions. Who wrote each one is not returned.
get.description: The conversation comments on a GitHub issue or pull request: text, dates and reactions. WHO WROTE EACH ONE IS NOT RETURNED -- login, avatar and profile url arrive in the response and are discarded, and so is author_association, which is an attribute of the person. Code REVIEW comments on a PR live at another endpoint and are not here. An empty list is an answer; an issue that does not exist is a real 404.

get.summary: List available niches and how much history each has
get.description: No API key required. Returns the niche labels and archive depth, never the archive itself.

get.summary: Historical series for one niche, grouped by item
get.description:
Grouped by ITEM, not by window. A window is how the archive stores; an item with a series is how the question is asked. Capped at 5000 series points and a 90-day span, both enforced in the database. When the cap is hit, `truncated` is true and the series is incomplete — narrow the interval rather than drawing conclusions from a partial series.

An unknown niche is NOT a 404: nothing validates the name, so a typo returns `items: []` with `points: 0` — AND still spends a call, because the quota counter increments before the archive is read. Resolve niche names at `/api/v1/nichos` first.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: ISO 8601. Defaults to 7 days ago.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: ISO 8601. Defaults to now.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Hint only. The hard cap lives in the database and a larger value here does not raise it.

paid_from.description: Which pocket paid: the monthly free allowance or purchased credits.

429.description: Monthly quota exhausted. The body carries `limit` and `renews_at`.

get.summary: What gained traction in a niche — charged only when it finds movement
get.description:
Costs 10 credits, and CHARGES ONLY IF IT FINDS MOVEMENT. An empty result is a 200 with `credits_charged: 0` and a `note` saying so, not an error and not a charge: the risk of an empty window sits with us, so you do not need defensive logic to avoid calling.

RANKED BY POINTS GAINED, NOT BY POSITION. This is the caveat that matters most, so it is stated before the parameters. Measured on 2026-09-06 across 19 pairs of windows: position changed for 19 of 29 items WITHOUT A SINGLE POINT CHANGING. Most items in a snapshot sit within a few points of each other, so ties are the rule, and a tie reshuffle looks exactly like movement if you read `position`. `points_gained` is Hacker News's own counter, not a number we derive, and it is what this endpoint sorts by.

`interval_min` IS THE REAL ELAPSED TIME between the two captures compared, not the window you asked for. The endpoint picks the archived window whose real capture time is closest to `hours` ago — windows are not equidistant, and observed intervals have ranged from 12 to 321 minutes. Asking `hours=24` against an archive that is 20 hours deep returns `interval_min: 1208`, not 1440. Divide by this number, not by the one you sent.

An unknown niche is NOT a 404 here: it produces the same empty, uncharged 200 as a quiet window. Confirm the niche exists at `/api/v1/nichos` before reading an empty result as 'nothing moved'.

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: How far back to look for the comparison window. A target, not a guarantee — the archive answers with the closest window it actually has, and reports the real gap in `interval_min`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Top N by points gained. Clamped to 100 in the database; a larger value here does not raise it.

200.description: OK — with movement (`credits_charged: 10`) or without it (`credits_charged: 0`, `items: []`, and a `note`). Both are successes; branch on `total`, not on the status code.

interval_min.description: Real minutes between the two captures compared. `null` when there was no movement to compare. A delta without an interval is a number without a unit — read this before reading `points_gained`.

credits_charged.description: Credits actually charged for this call. 0 when the result was empty.

credits_balance.description: Credits left on the key after this call.

note.description: Present only on an empty, uncharged result.
note.example: nothing gained traction in this window -- not charged

400.description: `parametro_invalido` — `hours` outside 1–720 or `limit` outside 1–100, or either one not an integer. Rejected before the call reaches the archive, so nothing is charged.

401.description: `chave_invalida` — missing, unknown or deactivated key. A missing `Authorization` header reports the same code as a wrong key: the database decides, and it cannot tell an absent key from one that does not exist. The response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`.

402.description: Not enough credits — `sem_creditos` (body carries `credits_balance` and `needed`) or `teto_estourado` (body carries `spent_this_month` and `cap`). 402 and not 429 on purpose: 429 means wait and retry, 402 means waiting will not help. Do not back off — top up or raise the ceiling.

503.description: `endpoint_indisponivel` — this endpoint is switched off at the database, not broken. Nothing charged.

bearerAuth.description: API key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer hk_live_...`. Quota is monthly and renews on the 1st. Unused quota does not roll over and does not expire mid-cycle — you get the whole month.

http.description: Echoed by errors that originate in the database. The real HTTP status is authoritative — do not branch on this field.

credits_balance.description: `sem_creditos` only: credits left on the key.

needed.description: `sem_creditos` only: credits the call would cost.

SeriesPoint.description: One observation of one item, in one hourly window.

window.description: Rounded to the hour. This is the bucket, not the exact capture time — two runs in the same hour share a window.

left_at.description: null while the item is still in the ranking.

movement.description: Oldest position minus newest. Positive means it climbed. Read this together with `points` in the series: a change of position with no change in points is a tie reshuffle, not a trend.

Mover.description: One item that GAINED points between the two compared windows. Items that lost points, and items present in only one of the two windows, are not in this list — losing is not traction, and an item with nothing to compare against has no delta.

points_gained.description: Newest score minus oldest. Always positive. THIS is the ranking key of the response — see the endpoint description for why it is not position.

position.description: Position in the newest window, carried for reference only. Do not rank by it and do not diff it across calls.

Author.description: The same twelve names on every platform. A field that does not exist there is null, never absent and never zero: zero is a fact about the account, null is a fact about our reading.

text_html.description: Mastodon only. Third-party HTML, unsanitised — sanitise before rendering or you have an XSS hole. `text` is the same content already stripped.

title.description: Always null: a status has no title.

position.description: Always null: chronological order is not a ranking.

thumbnail_url.description: Null on bluesky and mastodon — the image embed has not been measured on a large enough sample to promise a shape.

quotes.description: Null on threads: the source publishes none.

PostsEnvelope.description: Same envelope as every other route. `data.items` carries the posts the account itself wrote — reposts and boosts of other people are excluded by authorship. `has_more` is per platform, not one answer for all three: Bluesky computes it from the source cursor, Mastodon reports false until we read the `Link` header, and Threads reports null because its posts come inside the profile document and cannot be paged. A null is us saying we do not know, which is different from saying there is no more.

ProfileEnvelope.description: Identical shape on success and on error, so a client writes one parser. `success` is the only field that decides; `data` and `error` are mutually exclusive and the other is null, never absent.

type.description: Branch on this, never on the message text.

credits_remaining.description: THE SUM: purchased balance plus what is left of this month's free allowance. This is the only number that answers "can I call again" — it is not 0 while you can still call. null means we could not read it, which is not the same as zero.

free_credits_remaining.description: What is left of this month's free allowance.

free_credits_total.description: The monthly free allowance for this key.

free_credits_reset_at.description: When the free allowance resets: 00:00 UTC on the 1st. It is here so the sum dropping at the turn of the month is expected rather than a surprise.

cached.description: `true` is a promise that we did NOT charge: it always comes with `credits_used: 0`.
